description: Tier 3. Is the exporter's view of ISE current, and which source is serving each dataset? Read this before concluding that anything on the ISE dashboards is real.

panels.description: How many datasets both collected successfully and are inside their freshness window. This is the number that decides whether to believe the other nine dashboards.

targets.expr: count by (instance) ((((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1)) == 1)

panels.title: Datasets trustworthy

panels.description: Datasets that are enabled but currently either failing or stale. Every panel fed by one of these is blank or frozen somewhere in the set.

targets.expr: count by (instance) ((((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1)) == 0)

panels.title: Datasets not collecting

panels.description: Datasets being served by something other than their preferred source. Not a failure — the exporter is doing its job — but the data may be coarser or older than the design intended, and the reason table below says why.
panels.title: Datasets on a fallback provider

panels.description: Seconds since the least recently successful dataset last landed. The single worst-case staleness anywhere in the exporter's view of ISE.
panels.title: Oldest successful collection

panels.description: The longest current run of consecutive failures on any dataset. One failure is noise; a run means something is broken rather than flaky, and the failure table below has the error text.
panels.title: Worst consecutive failures

panels.description: Which exporter version is running and which ISE release it was built to target. A mismatch between this and the appliance's actual release is the first thing to check when panels are unexpectedly empty.
panels.title: Exporter build

panels.description: One lane per dataset, green while that dataset was both collecting and fresh. Every unexplained step, gap or plateau on any other dashboard should be checked against this panel before it is treated as an ISE event.

targets.expr: ((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (instance,dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment"} == 1))) == bool 1)

panels.title: Dataset trustworthiness over time

panels.description: Every dataset with whether it is up and fresh, how long since it last succeeded, how long its collection takes, and when it runs next. Read 'Age' against 'Since attempt': the two far apart means the dataset is being attempted and failing, the two together means it simply has not run.
panels.title: Dataset status

panels.description: The most recent failure each dataset recorded, with the reason and the detail text the exporter captured from ISE. Empty is healthy. This is the panel that turns 'collection failed' into something specific enough to act on.
panels.title: Latest failure per dataset

panels.description: Which provider each dataset is using, whether that is a downgrade from the preferred one, and the reason the exporter recorded for choosing it. The whole argument for this exporter's design is that a source change is visible rather than silent — this is where it is visible.
panels.title: Provider selection and fallback reason

panels.description: Providers configured for a dataset that the exporter could not use. Each row is a capability the deployment was configured to have and does not — usually a licence, a credential, or a schema the appliance does not expose.
panels.title: Declared but unusable providers

panels.description: Failure rate per dataset and reason. The consecutive-failure stat above says whether something is broken now; this says how often it has been breaking and for which stated reason, which is what separates a flaky appliance from a misconfiguration.
panels.title: Collection failures by reason

panels.description: Query rate against the Oracle reporting views, split by result. Failures here mean the reporting datasets fall back or go stale; the schema-gap table below usually explains them.
panels.title: Data Connect statements

panels.description: How long each reporting query is taking. Duration rising across all views is the appliance under load; one view rising alone is usually that view's data volume growing past what the current scan window can handle.
panels.title: Data Connect statement duration by view

panels.description: Whether each Data Connect view exists in this appliance's schema at all, whether it has rows, whether it has recent ones, and how old its newest row is. A view that stops advancing makes every panel fed from it silently stale rather than obviously broken; a view that does not exist is a capability this release does not have.
panels.title: Reporting source freshness

panels.description: Columns this exporter wants that the appliance's Data Connect schema does not provide. Each row is a panel somewhere in the set that will be empty or coarser than designed, named at the column level rather than guessed at.
panels.title: Schema capability gaps

panels.description: REST and OpenAPI traffic the exporter is generating, with the error rate beside it. Errors climbing here precede datasets falling back to a different provider.
panels.title: ISE API request and error rate

panels.description: How long the appliance is taking to answer, by API. Rising latency here is the earliest warning that collection durations and then freshness are about to suffer.
panels.title: ISE API latency, 95th percentile

panels.description: Whether the pxGrid stream is connected, how many sessions it is tracking, how long since the last frame, and how often it has reconnected in this window. A silent but connected stream is the failure mode worth catching here; repeated reconnects mean it is flapping rather than working.
panels.title: pxGrid session stream

panels.description: How much of each entity list the exporter has full detail for. Panels fed from a cache are suppressed below 99% so they cannot under-report beside a complete neighbour — a dip here is the explanation for a table that has gone blank.
panels.title: Detail-cache coverage

panels.description: How many entities each cache is holding. Read beside coverage: entries flat while coverage falls means the entity list grew and the cache has not caught up yet, which is normal after a bulk import and a problem if it persists.
panels.title: Detail-cache size

panels.description: Breakdowns where the exporter published fewer groups than ISE reported, and by how much. Truncation is a deliberate cost control, but it must never be silent: this table is where the cost of that bound is stated.
panels.title: Bounded breakdown truncation

panels.description: Per-target queue depth and whether the lane is busy. A queue that does not drain means the exporter is asking for more than the appliance will answer in the time available, and freshness will slip next.
panels.title: Scheduler lanes

panels.description: Per-entity detail fetches by result, with how many were deferred. Deferrals are the budget working as designed; failures are not, and they are what stops a cache reaching the coverage floor.
panels.title: Detail fetch outcomes

panels.description: Which optional breakdown dimensions the appliance's schema actually populates. A dimension marked unpopulated is one whose panel elsewhere in the set will be empty by design — a capability limit stated plainly rather than a graph that silently never fills.
panels.title: Populated breakdown dimensions

panels.description: How many network devices the directory holds, how many activity records it could attribute to one, and how old the activity source is. Unattributed activity is why some per-device panels have an 'unknown' row.

targets.expr: (ise3_nad_activity_source_age_seconds{instance=~"$deployment"}) and on(instance) (((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="nad_health"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="nad_health"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="nad_health"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="nad_health"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: NAD directory attribution

panels.description: Share of authentications that carried a usable latency measurement, and how many samples the reconstructed latency figures are drawn from. Every latency panel in the set is only as trustworthy as these two numbers.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: avg by (instance) ((ise3_radius_authentication_latency_coverage{instance=~"$deployment"}) and on(instance) (((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="radius_reporting"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="radius_reporting"} == 1))) == 1)))

(ise3_session_authentication_latency_samples{instance=~"$deployment"}) and on(instance) (((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="session_authorization"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="session_authorization"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="session_authorization"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Latency measurement coverage

panels.description: How many endpoints the live attribute feed published, how many internal TACACS accounts could be classified, and how much state the exporter is holding on disk. Low publication or classification means the corresponding breakdowns are drawn from a subset.

targets.expr: (ise3_endpoint_attributes_published{instance=~"$deployment"}) and on(instance) (((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="endpoint_attributes"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="endpoint_attributes"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="endpoint_attributes"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="endpoint_attributes"} == 1))) == 1))

(ise3_tacacs_internal_accounts_classified{instance=~"$deployment"}) and on(instance) (((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_up{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="tacacs_config"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="tacacs_config"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max by (instance) (ise3_dataset_fresh{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="tacacs_config"} and on(instance,dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{instance=~"$deployment",dataset="tacacs_config"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Attribute and classification coverage

panels.description: Rate at which the exporter had to substitute characters the appliance returned in an encoding it declared but did not honour. Non-zero is not fatal, but it means some label values on the reporting dashboards are approximations of what ISE actually holds.
panels.title: Characters replaced in Data Connect results

panels.description: Purpose, reading order, and where to go next. Kept with the dashboard so the meaning cannot drift away from the panels.

options.content:
**Purpose** — answer one question — is the exporter's view of ISE current enough to believe? Everything here is about the exporter, not about ISE.

**Read it in this order**

1. Read the trust strip and the trustworthiness timeline.
2. For anything not trustworthy, read its row in **Dataset status** and then **Latest failure**.
3. If a dataset is on a fallback provider, read why in the provider table before treating the data as wrong.

**When something is red**

- Schema gaps: the appliance does not expose what a panel needs — that is a capability limit, not a bug.
- Queue depth not draining or API latency rising: the exporter is asking for more than ISE will answer — see the Load dashboard.
- Cache coverage low: dependent panels are suppressed on purpose and will return on their own.

**Related dashboards** — Triage, Exporter load, Control plane

*Owner: set this to the team that answers the page. Runbook: link it here — a red panel with no runbook is a puzzle, not an alert.*
